text:
kevin: hitting 400 when calling tool with JSON args after our CLI upgrade — this used to work. pasted curl below.
kevin: curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"tool":"convert","args":"{\"path\":\"C:\\new\\folder\\input.txt\",}"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/toolcall
amanda (support): thanks kevin — that's a helpful repro. can you paste the exact error body from the API? status/code?
kevin: response: 400 Bad Request, body: {"error":"invalid_tool_arguments","detail":"JSON parse error at position 45: unexpected token '}'"}
amanda (support): looks like two issues: unescaped backslashes in a JSON string and a trailing comma before the object close. CLI looks like it double-wraps the args JSON as a string. can you try escaping backslashes and removing the trailing comma? e.g.:
```
-d '{"tool":"convert","args":{"path":"C:\\new\\folder\\input.txt"}}'
```
kevin: tried that locally and it worked, but our app still sends the old form after the upgrade. app builds arg string in shell. snippet: 
```
ARGS="{\"path\":\"$FILE_PATH\",}"
curl ... -d '{"tool":"convert","args":"'$ARGS'"}'
```
amanda (support): aha — you're embedding JSON as a string inside another JSON value which causes double-encoding plus the stray comma. you should send args as a JSON object (not a JSON-encoded string) and remove the trailing comma. this is a common shell construction pitfall.
devon (cli): filing a quick note — our CLI regressed and treated --args as a raw string, skipping validation. reproducer: Windows-style paths with single backslashes get under-escaped and then the CLI added another layer. i'll open a PR to validate/normalize.
ingrid (runtime): can you attach the exact request headers and body text (we need Content-Type and the raw body) and confirm client version? we saw similar in another thread but slightly different.
kevin: headers: Content-Type: application/json, User-Agent: ourapp/2.1.3; raw body: {"tool":"convert","args":"{\"path\":\"C:\new\folder\input.txt\",}"} 
amanda (support): thanks — sharing with eng. assigning to @devon and @ingrid. in the meantime, workaround: build JSON safely (avoid manual string concat) or escape path with doubled backslashes, or use jq: 
```
jq -n --arg p "$FILE_PATH" '{tool: "convert", args: {path: $p}}'
```
kevin: jq workaround works for us, thanks. quick question: should the API accept stringified JSON in args? previous integration apparently sent it as a string and worked.
ingrid (runtime): API expects args to be a JSON object/array per tool schema. stringified JSON was tolerated in some legacy paths but causes schema validation failures for strict tools. i'll open ticket RT-1024 to make the error message clearer and document the expected shape.
amanda (support): i'll update the KB with a short note about shell pitfalls and link to the jq example + the incoming ticket. kevin: do you want us to sanitize server-side to accept the old form?
ingrid (runtime): prefer client fixes, but we can add an enterprise lenient-parse flag behind a feature toggle if customers need a temporary bridge.
kevin: appreciated, we'll roll the client patch. :thumbsup:
